sovereign_country.strategic_role: 全球跨境基金设立第一大国、超大型跨国投资架构

business_scope.primary_industry_name: Private Investment Holding for High-Net-Worth Family Assets

meta_jurisdiction_context.jurisdiction_name_en: Luxembourg (unitary national jurisdiction, no sub-state tax distinction)
meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Civil Law (continental European) with strong supranational EU law overlay and hybrid treaty-driven corporate governance
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: Treaty on the Functioning of the European Union (freedom of establishment under Article 49 TFEU and free movement of capital under Article 63 TFEU)
EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive 2011/96/EU as amended by Directive (EU) 2015/121
Belgo-Luxembourg Economic Union (BLEU) bilateral investment treaty network, including BLEU-China (2005), BLEU-Hong Kong (1998), BLEU-Singapore (2010), and BLEU-UAE (2009)

Double Taxation Agreements relevant to family-office asset holding, including Luxembourg-Hong Kong (2008), Luxembourg-Singapore (1993 as amended), Luxembourg-UAE (2009), and Luxembourg-USA (1996 as amended by the 2009 Protocol)
OECD Multilateral Convention to Implement Tax Treaty Related Measures to Prevent BEPS (MLI), signed by Luxembourg on 7 June 2017 and ratified on 1 March 2021

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Law of 12 November 2004 on the fight against money laundering and terrorist financing, as amended notably by the Law of 25 March 2020 implementing the Fifth Anti-Money Laundering Directive; Law of 13 January 2019 establishing the Register of Beneficial Owners (RBE, Registre des bénéficiaires effectifs), as amended; CSSF Regulation No. 12-02 of 14 December 2012, as amended; Law of 10 August 1915 on Commercial Companies, as amended; and Law of 19 December 2002 on the Register of Commerce and Companies (RCS).
ubo_and_aml_profiling.ubo_disclosure_level: Government_Only_Access (public access restricted since the Luxembourg Constitutional Court decision of 9 July 2020; access limited to the Luxembourg FIU, the CSSF, tax authorities and AMF/CFT obliged entities with legitimate interest)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Current extract from the commercial register of the founding corporate shareholder (extrait du registre de commerce)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent commercial registry of the founder's country of origin; for Luxembourg founders, the Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing of the founding corporate shareholder (certificat de bonne tenue ou d'existence legale)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent corporate registry or government agency of the founder's country of origin

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified board or shareholders resolution of the ultimate parent entity approving the incorporation of the Luxembourg SARL and the appointment of its managers
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Board of directors or general meeting of the parent entity
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille on the certified extract

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified copy of the passport of each UBO, director and proposed SARL manager
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary public in the individual's country of nationality or domicile
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarized copy followed by Hague Apostille

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Original bank reference letter for the SFO founder and ultimate beneficial owners
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Private bank or credit institution maintaining accounts of the founder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Original on bank letterhead; apostille or consular legalization required in enhanced risk cases

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all UBOs, managers and signatories under the AML/CFT Law of 12 November 2004 (as amended) and CSSF Regulation No. 12-02, including: PEP status and close associates or family members; United Nations Security Council and EU autonomous consolidated sanctions lists (EU Regulation 269/2014 and EU Regulation 2580/2001); domestic CSSF and CRF (FIU) risk alerts and adverse media; and, because the target rails include USD private banking wires, contractual OFAC SDN and non-SDN screening by US correspondent banks. The SFO is classified medium-risk enhanced, triggering source-of-wealth and source-of-funds documentation for each UBO.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) – RCS e-Filing Platform, accessible at www.lbr.lu and via guichet.lu
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Name clearance and all RCS filings are processed in French using Latin script. The corporate name must be available in the Luxembourg business name database and must not be misleading; non-Latin names, including Chinese family-office trade names, must be rendered in a phonetic French transliteration approved by the RCS, while the registered name must be reproducible in the French-language company statutes.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Banque (requires CSSF banking licence before reservation)
Fonds, FCP, SICAV, SICAR (regulated investment vehicle terms requiring prior CSSF authorisation)
Société d'investissement (restricted to regulated collective investment undertakings)
Bourse, Values mobilières, Courtier (regulated financial market terms)
Luxembourg or its derivatives in a manner suggesting state affiliation (requires prior ministerial approval)
Mémorial, Gouvernement, Administration (state or official body references)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon rejection, the applicant may immediately refile a name reservation with a revised name or file an appeal with the Luxembourg District Court (Tribunal d'arrondissement de Luxembourg, Commercial Chamber) within the statutory appeal period, generally one month from notification of the registrar's refusal, per the Law of 19 December 2002 on the Register of Commerce and Companies. The appellant must submit a formal notice of appeal followed by a written memorandum; legal representation is strongly recommended. Where the rejection is based on a sensitive token, the applicant must first obtain the prior ministerial or CSSF authorisation before refiling.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Statutory domiciliation is permissible under the Law of 31 May 1999 on the Domiciliation of Companies, as amended, but only through a licensed or registered domiciliation agent in Luxembourg. A pure virtual office may satisfy RCS registration requirements for an unlicensed single-family-office SARL, but it will attract heightened scrutiny by Luxembourg tax authorities, credit institutions and auditors for tax residency and commercial substance purposes; a passive letterbox arrangement is fiscally and reputationally inadvisable.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low for an unlicensed passive SFO, estimated at 5-10 percent annual probability of unannounced inspection by the Luxembourg direct tax administration or social security authorities during data-matching controls; probability rises above 50 percent if regulated activities are detected, if suspicious transactions are flagged, or if the SFO becomes subject to CSSF enforcement.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Name availability search and reservation of the dénomination sociale with the Luxembourg Business Registers
Notarial deed of incorporation of the SARL including drafting of the articles of association before a Luxembourg notary
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Regulated notarial tariff plus statutory disbursements

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: RCS registration filing for the newly incorporated SARL
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory registration tariff per the RCS fee schedule

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Publication of the incorporation instrument in the Recueil des Sociétés et Associations (RSA)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Luxembourg Ministry of Justice through LBR publication platform

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Initial UBO declaration preparation and filing with the Luxembourg Register of Beneficial Owners (RBE)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (RBE); statutory filing free of charge
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market benchmark for counsel compliance processing; no statutory fee

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Apostille or consular legalization of founding shareholder documents and certified copies (bundle of five documents)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Luxembourg Ministry of Foreign Affairs or consular post of document origin
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Hague Apostille per-document fee of approximately USD 40-60; consular fee schedules outside the Hague Convention

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Certified translation of foundation documents into French by a sworn translator (approximately 20 pages)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market benchmark of EUR 50-75 per page

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Pre-incorporation due diligence report, UBO piercing analysis, PEP and sanctions screening, and source-of-wealth review
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market benchmark for a fixed-fee single-family-office setup

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: First-year registered office domiciliation deposit under the Law of 31 May 1999 through a licensed domiciliation agent
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market benchmark of EUR 150-300 per month

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Bank reference letters and enhanced KYC documentation package for pre-opening of private banking and custody accounts
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market benchmark for bank documentation and AML/CFT customer due diligence package

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Luxembourg Law of 10 August 1915 on Commercial Companies, as amended (Loi modifiée du 10 août 1915 concernant les sociétés commerciales), Articles 710-1 et seq. governing the Société à Responsabilité Limitée (SARL); Law of 19 December 2002 on the Register of Commerce and Companies and the Accounting Records and Annual Accounts of Undertakings; Law of 2 September 2011 regulating access to the professions of craftsman, merchant, industrialist and certain liberal professions.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS) operated by Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR), with mandatory prior execution of the constitutive deed before a Luxembourg notary (Chambre des Notaires du Grand-Duché de Luxembourg).
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Notarial deed of incorporation and articles of association (acte constitutif / statuts) executed before a Luxembourg notary, electronically filed with the RCS, and subsequently published in the Recueil électronique des sociétés et associations (RESA).
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: Statutory minimum share capital of EUR 12,500, fully subscribed at incorporation; cash contributions must be paid up to at least 25% of each share's nominal value at incorporation, with the balance payable within five years, although full payment is market practice for an SFO; the capital must be blocked on a Luxembourg bank account and evidenced by a certificate of capital blocking (attestation de blocage de fonds) delivered to the notary; contributions in kind require a valuation report from an independent statutory auditor (réviseur d'entreprises agréé).
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: FIRST BOARD RESOLUTION OF [SARL NAME] S.À R.L. — Unanimously adopted by the sole shareholder acting as the general meeting on [DATE]: (1) RESOLVED that the subscription of [NUMBER] shares, nominal value EUR [VALUE] each, for an aggregate capital of EUR [AMOUNT] credited to the blocked capital account, is ratified; (2) RESOLVED that the registered office be fixed at [ADDRESS], Luxembourg, and lease execution be delegated; (3) RESOLVED that [MANAGER NAME] be appointed Manager (Gérant), acting singly, with full authority to open and operate bank accounts, sign contracts, and represent the company; (4) RESOLVED that the said Manager be authorized to complete RCS registration, RESA publication, tax and employer registrations, RBE filing, and all ancillary formalities, with specimen signature valid for filings.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Company name check and blocking of share capital on a Luxembourg escrow account
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg credit institution (private bank or national bank) acting jointly with the founding shareholder and the appointed Luxembourg notary
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Instruct the notary to run a negative name search against the RCS database for the proposed SFO corporate name. Open a blocked funds account at a Luxembourg bank in the name of the future SARL and transfer at least the minimum capital of EUR 12,500 with the reference purpose of share capital blocking. Obtain the bank's certificate of capital blocking (attestation de blocage de fonds) addressed to the notary. The funds remain immobilized until the RCS delivers the registration certificate, whereupon the bank releases the funds to the company's operational current account.
required_dossiers: Bank KYC file comprising certified passport copy of the founding shareholder and any ultimate beneficial owner
Description of the intended single-family-office activity (ISIC 6430 / NAICS 525920)
Proof of source of funds for the cash contribution
Draft articles of association and business plan
RCS name availability confirmation issued by the notary
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank refuses account opening on AML grounds, supplement the source-of-wealth file with portfolio statements, tax returns or deed of gift and resubmit; if still refused, approach an alternative Luxembourg credit institution and restart the escrow process with corrected KYC documentation, which does not delay notarial drafting.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Execution before a Luxembourg notary of the deed of incorporation and articles of association
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg notary (Chambre des Notaires du Grand-Duché de Luxembourg)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The notary reviews the draft statutes for compliance with Article 710-1 et seq. of the Law of 10 August 1915, verifies the name availability, the capital blocking certificate, the KYC documentation and, where a contribution in kind is proposed, obtains a valuation report from an independent réviseur d'entreprises agréé. The founding shareholder or its attorney-in-fact signs the notarial deed and the share subscription list. Legal personality of the SARL arises upon signature of the deed, subject to subsequent RCS registration.
required_dossiers: Executed draft articles of association and subscription list
Certificate of capital blocking issued by the Luxembourg bank
Certified passport copies and proof of residential address of the shareholder and the manager
Criminal record extract (acte n° 3 or foreign equivalent) for each manager
Corporate authorizations and board minutes of any corporate shareholder
Registered office lease agreement and landlord's written consent
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary identifies deficiencies in the ownership chain, source of funds or statutory clauses, the shareholder supplies the requested corroborating documents within the notary's deadline; the deed is then executed on the next available date without amendment of the economic substance of the structure.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Registration of the company in the Luxembourg Trade and Companies Register (RCS)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS) / Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) electronic filing portal
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The notary or the delegated manager tele-files the notarial deed together with the RCS incorporation declaration forms, the manager's acceptance of office, specimen signatures, and the declaration concerning the Law of 2 September 2011 (business establishment permit or exemption). Once accepted, the RCS attributes a national registration number and issues the corporate extract (extrait), which constitutes definitive proof of incorporation and legal personality.
required_dossiers: RCS incorporation declaration forms (including natural-person data of the manager)
Declaration of exemption under the Law of 2 September 2011 for a pure holding / single-family-office activity
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the RCS issues a request for further information (demande de complément), respond through the LBR portal within the stated deadline; if the objection concerns statutory content, execute a rectificative notarial deed and re-file; the incorporation remains valid in the interim.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Administration des contributions directes (ACD) for direct taxes; Administration de l'enregistrement, des domaines et de la TVA (AEDT) for VAT; unified e-services via MyGuichet.lu
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A foreign investor must first incorporate a Luxembourg entity (SARL) before a notary and register with the Luxembourg Business Registers (RCS). The RCS registration triggers automatic attribution of a national taxpayer number (numéro de matricule). If the entity engages in taxable supplies of goods/services in Luxembourg, separate VAT registration is filed with the AEDT through Form 640 or via MyGuichet.lu; non-resident entities with no place of business in Luxembourg must appoint a Luxembourg VAT fiscal representative for VAT registration. The VAT ID (TVA number) is issued after evidence of taxable activity and, where applicable, posting of security.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No check-the-box or pass-through election exists for a Luxembourg SARL. However, a SARL may apply to form a VAT group (assujetti unique) with Luxembourg subsidiaries, and may elect Luxembourg fiscal unity (intégration fiscale) for corporate income tax and municipal business tax if the parent holds at least 95% of the subsidiary. Hybrid mismatch elections are constrained by anti-hybrid rules implementing ATAD (EU Directive 2016/1164), and no elective hybrid treatment is available for a standard single-family office.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: VAT (TVA — Taxe sur la Valeur Ajoutée)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: EUR 35,000 annual taxable turnover (excluding VAT) for mandatory VAT registration of established Luxembourg businesses; EUR 10,000 annual cross-border distance-sale threshold for EU suppliers; no threshold for non-established suppliers of B2B services (reverse charge).
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: No real-time fiscal clearance or digital stamping regime. Electronic invoicing is mandatory for B2G supplies (via PEPPOL/UBL); B2B invoices may be issued electronically by mutual consent. VAT-registered persons must file periodic recapitulative statements (EC sales lists) and VAT returns electronically through the AEDT portal. There is no requirement for real-time API validation or digital stamping from a fiscal device.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Supplies of goods physically dispatched or transported outside Luxembourg and outside the EU are zero-rated (0%) if the supplier retains proof of export. Supplies of services to non-EU businesses are generally zero-rated where the recipient is a taxable person and effective use/exploitation is outside the EU; financial services and asset management supplied to an SFO remain exempt without credit rather than zero-rated. For goods, the supplier must obtain export confirmation from customs. For VAT-reclaim by non-established businesses, the 13th Directive/8th Directive refund procedures apply.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs export declaration (SAD/EX) / electronic ECS confirmation
Bill of Lading / Air Waybill / CMR transport document
Inward remittance certificate / proof of payment
Evidence of transport from Luxembourg to destination outside the EU
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Luxembourg VAT authorities may reassess zero-rating within the normal limitation period (5 years, extended to 10 years in case of fraud). Fraudulent export claims are subject to administrative penalties up to 100% of the tax evaded (usually 10%-50% depending on good faith), and criminal sanctions for tax fraud (imprisonment and fines) under the General Tax Law and LJF. Retroactive clawback of unjustified zero-rating plus default interest at the statutory rate is routinely applied upon insufficient documentation or missing intra-EU/export proof.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banque centrale du Luxembourg (BCL) is the national central bank of Luxembourg within the Eurosystem; the BCL is the competent authority for balance-of-payments statistical reporting, foreign-exchange reserve management, and compliance with European Central Bank regulations. The Commission de Surveillance du Secteur Financier (CSSF) supervises credit institutions and enforces anti-money laundering and customer due diligence requirements under the Luxembourg AML Law of 25 March 2020 and CSSF Regulation 12-02.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Luxembourg operates a fully open capital and current account regime under EU law (Article 63 TFEU). The euro is freely convertible for all transactions, including capital injections, trade settlements, dividend remittances, and liquidation proceeds. There are no exchange-control permits, no prior central-bank approvals, and no currency quotas; the only practical frictions are (i) documentary proof of source of funds under AML/KYC rules and (ii) withholding tax compliance for outbound dividends (15% domestic Luxembourg withholding tax, reduced under tax treaties or eliminated under the EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive).
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: None. Luxembourg imposes no statutory surrender timeline, no mandatory conversion ratio, and no repatriation deadline for export receipts. A resident SARL may lawfully retain export proceeds in any currency; the only administrative obligation is the BCL/ECB balance-of-payments statistical reporting for cross-border transactions above the applicable reporting threshold (generally EUR 12,500 per transaction or monthly cumulative amount), which the servicing bank files on the client's behalf.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Banque et Caisse d'Épargne de l'État (BCEE)

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital Escrow Account / Private Banking Custody

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility: Low to Medium. EU-licensed e-money institutions (EMIs) and payment institutions established in Luxembourg (Law of 14 April 2011 on e-money institutions; Law of 10 November 2009 on payment services) can offer payment accounts and SEPA/SWIFT rail access, but they cannot provide regulatory securities custody, credit lines, letters of credit, or FX hedging, and client funds are safeguarded outside the Luxembourg deposit guarantee scheme (FGDL). An offshore non-EU EMI has no EU passporting rights and cannot lawfully serve as the primary treasury bank for a Luxembourg SARL without a Luxembourg/EU branch; EMIs should be used only as a temporary operational collection bridge, never for capital escrow or custody of family investment assets.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Physical presence is the market-standard baseline: Luxembourg tier-1 banks almost uniformly require an in-person interview with at least one authorised signatory and the ultimate beneficial owner (UBO, holding 25% or more or exercising effective control) before opening corporate accounts. Remote onboarding is legally possible under eIDAS-compliant video identification and CSSF Regulation 12-02, and some banks permit hybrid video verification for EU tax-resident clients; however, for non-EU UBOs and higher-risk profiles, banks require a physical interview at the Luxembourg head office, a correspondent branch, or a consulate with notarised and apostilled identity documents. For a single-family office, compliance committees will also require the directors to explain the family's source of wealth, the commercial purpose of the SARL, and the absence of third-party asset management activity.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Complex multi-layer ownership chain (holding companies, trusts, or foundations) concealing the ultimate beneficial owner.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Apostilled/legalised organisational chart; notarial certificates and RCS extracts for each corporate layer; certified identity documents; source-of-wealth and source-of-funds declarations; trust deed or equivalent fiduciary instrument; confirmation from the registered agent that nominee/trustee roles are legitimate; and a written explanation of the bona fide tax and succession-planning purpose of the structure.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual General Meeting approval of annual accounts
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Shareholders of the SARL under the Law of 10 August 1915 and the Articles of Association
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within six months after each financial year-end for a calendar-year SARL; by 30 June unless extended by court order
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late approval exposes managers to civil and corporate liability; does not attract a direct administrative fine but triggers later annual accounts filing non-compliance risk.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual financial statements (annual accounts) filing with the Luxembourg Trade and Companies Register
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) / Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within seven months after the financial year-end and no later than one month after approval by the Annual General Meeting; for calendar-year SARL, by 31 July
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Persistent failure may result in court-imposed penalties, administrative strike-off from the RCS after judicial order, and publication of the default in the electronic register; directors and managers may be held personally liable.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Corporate income tax, municipal business tax, and net wealth tax annual returns (liasse fiscale)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Filing deadline is set by the annual declaration notice issued by the ACD; for calendar-year entities generally 31 May of the following year when no extension is requested
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing may trigger statutory late-payment interest (currently 6.9% p.a.), surcharges on assessed taxes, administrative fines, and criminal prosecution for deliberate non-compliance.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual UBO confirmation (annual confirmation of beneficial owner register data)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers – Register of Beneficial Owners (RBE)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually during the month corresponding to the anniversary of the RCS registration; any share transfer changing UBO must be declared within one month
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Non-compliance with the UBO Law of 13 January 2019 may result in monetary fines up to EUR 50,000 for legal entities and potential criminal penalties for officers; repeat failures increase exposure.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Statutory auditor's report (rapport du réviseur d'entreprises agréé) when the audit threshold is triggered
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Shareholders at the Annual General Meeting; report is filed with the RCS together with the annual accounts
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Issued in time for the Annual General Meeting and filed with the annual accounts within the seven-month deadline after the financial year-end
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to obtain a required auditor's report may invalidate the approval of accounts, expose management to liability, and lead to court-ordered appointment of a réviseur and administrative sanctions.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Mandatory if the SARL exceeds two of the following three criteria on two consecutive balance-sheet dates: total balance sheet EUR 4.4 million, net turnover EUR 8.8 million, average of 50 full-time-equivalent employees; a single-family-office SARL with balance-sheet assets exceeding EUR 4.4 million is in scope.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Luxembourg GAAP ('Lux GAAP') as codified by the Law of 19 December 2002 implementing Directive 2013/34/EU; IFRS may be used for consolidated financial statements, but statutory solo annual accounts remain under Lux GAAP.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Under the Law of 13 January 2019, every Luxembourg entity must hold a beneficial owner register and confirm the accuracy of UBO data annually during the month of the anniversary of the RCS registration; any transfer of shares that changes the beneficial owner must be reported within one month. The annual confirmation must specifically reconcile shareholding transfers during the preceding 12 months and update the UBO filing accordingly.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Minute Book (minutes of shareholders' meetings and board decisions)

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 3,500 - USD 8,500 per year for registered-office services, resident agent and corporate secretarial support from a Luxembourg fiduciary or PFS firm
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 8,500 - USD 22,000 for a single-family-office SARL with moderate portfolio complexity; higher for entities with significant investment holdings

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 25.94% (Luxembourg City, tax year 2025: 18% CIT + 7% solidarity surcharge = 1.26 points + 6.75% municipal business tax; for tax year 2024 the aggregate was 24.94% at 17% CIT).
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Participation exemption (100% exemption of qualifying dividends and capital gains under LIR Art. 166/166bis); IP box (80% exemption of qualifying IP income, nexus-ratio limited); 50% exemption for non-qualifying?; minimum net wealth tax regime for holding companies (IFL at 0.05% on exempt shareholdings); deduction for investment (8% investment tax credit).
